$comment: The five events this deployment is permitted to record. The program owner's brief says 'record the five defined events' but no definition exists in the materials available to this session (FLG-015), so these five are proposed: the collector rejects every other name, and the front end only emits these. Renaming or replacing the list is a one-file change that the gate then enforces everywhere.
privacy_rules: no IP address is stored, read or logged
no cookie and no local identifier beyond the browser's own session queue
no third-party endpoint receives a request
navigator.doNotTrack or the global privacy control signal stops collection before the first event
the page path is stored, never the query string, so a tagged outbound URL cannot leak a session token into the log
retention is the append-only file; there is no user-level profile to delete

storage.rotation: one file per UTC day; the ledger ingests daily

events.name: page_view
events.fires_on: a guide, gear, cluster or summary page finishes loading

properties.referring_path: string, same-site only, empty for unknown

events.decision_it_serves: which entry pages bring strangers in, which decides where internal links and the next topic go
events.conversion_role: denominator for every rate in the ledger

events.name: product_link_click
events.fires_on: a click on any link carrying data-outbound, i.e. every tagged Amazon link
events.decision_it_serves: the only signal that says a page made someone want to look at a listing; separates a read page from a useful one
events.conversion_role: the numerator of click-through; joins to Amazon's click report by date, not by user

events.name: comparison_started
events.fires_on: two products selected in the comparison filter form
events.decision_it_serves: which pairings readers actually want side by side, which is what decides the next comparison page
events.conversion_role: intent signal ahead of a click; the highest-value editorial input in the set

events.name: checklist_item_toggled
events.fires_on: a buyer checks a line in a decision checklist
events.decision_it_serves: which criteria people actually use, which is how a guide earns its next revision without guessing
events.conversion_role: engagement depth; correlates with return visits more reliably than time on page

events.name: email_signup_submitted
events.fires_on: the reader-capture form is submitted, whether or not capture is enabled
events.decision_it_serves: demand for a list before we take on storing addresses; today it measures interest in something we cannot yet deliver, which is exactly the number we need
events.conversion_role: owned-audience growth; independent of any search system

not_collected: scroll depth and time on page, which are the two most commonly collected numbers with the least decision attached

amazon_side_metrics.clicks_and_orders: Associates Central reports are the authorized first-party source; nothing on this site claims an order count that did not come from them
amazon_side_metrics.ledger_join: by UTC date, never by user; the two systems share no identifier
amazon_side_metrics.note: The five defined events above are the on-site half. 'Reported orders' and 'eligible sessions' exist only in Amazon's reports, so the campaign ledger starts empty by design: data/ledger/campaign_ledger.csv.
